key: And the LORD said unto Moses: ‘Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; sweet spices with pure frankincense; of each shall there be a like weight.
s: Giving the recipe for the incense burnt before the testimony, God names its spices; Rashi, on Exodus 30:34, reads the foul-smelling galbanum among the spices as teaching that transgressors in Israel are to be counted with the community in its fasts and prayers.

evidence.words: וחלבנה. בֹּשֶׂם שֶׁרֵיחוֹ רַע, וְקוֹרִין לוֹ גַלְבְּנָא, וּמְנָאָהּ הַכָּתוּב בֵּין סַמָּנֵי הַקְּטֹרֶת לְלַמְּדֵנוּ שֶׁלֹּא יֵקַל בְּעֵינֵינוּ לְצָרֵף עִמָּנוּ בַּאֲגֻדַּת תַּעֲנִיּוֹתֵינוּ וּתְפִלּוֹתֵנוּ אֶת פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִמְנִין עִמָּנוּ
evidence.gloss: And galbanum: a spice whose smell is bad, called galbana; Scripture counted it among the spices of the incense to teach us that it should not be a light thing in our eyes to join with us, in the gathering of our fasts and prayers, the transgressors of Israel, so that they are counted with us.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Exodus 30:34, at [79,34]). Plain sense faithful: 30:34 to 38 give the composition of the holy incense, which 30:36 sets before the testimony in the tent of meeting (and 30:1 to 8 burn on the incense altar before the veil). Rashi’s comment on וחלבנה says the ill-smelling spice is counted among the incense spices to teach that the transgressors of Israel should be joined and counted with the congregation in its fasts and prayers: the sentence carries this without drift (it compresses ‘not to take lightly’ into ‘are to be counted’, which is the comment’s point). Evidence copied exactly from the packet’s Hebrew; gate ok.
